messages.content:
The issue is with the `FastDateFormat.getInstance` method not respecting the locale when outputting the week of the year in the format. The method `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String pattern, TimeZone timeZone, Locale locale)` is used to get an instance of `FastDateFormat` with the specified pattern, time zone, and locale. However, the problem lies in the implementation of this method.

The `getInstance` method creates an `emptyFormat` of `FastDateFormat` using the provided pattern, time zone, and locale. It then checks if an instance with the same properties exists in the `cInstanceCache`, and if not, it initializes the format and adds it to the cache before returning it.

In the failing test `testLang645`, a `FastDateFormat` instance is created with a pattern `"EEEE', week 'ww"` and a specific locale `"sv", "SE"`. The expected result is `"fredag, week 53"`, indicating Friday of the 53rd week. However, due to the issue with locale not being respected, the actual result might differ based on the system locale settings.

To fix the issue, the `FastDateFormat.getInstance` method needs to ensure that the locale is properly respected when formatting the date, especially when dealing with components like week of the year that are locale-sensitive.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The best locations to fix this issue would be:
```
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat.getInstance(String, TimeZone, Locale)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
